column1: # G4 phase 2: refer(t?) -- the CHECKED, TYPED, LINK-SHAPED reference
# string-valued field: the string must be an ENTITY ADDRESS, the
# addressed node must exist in the evaluation, and -- when `t` is given
# -- `t` is unified INTO the target. The field's own value stays the
# This is the piece a plain reference cannot be. `$.a.b` resolves by
# CLONING its target into place, so the row `link-vs-plain-ref` below
# generates a full copy of the auth node where the author meant a name;
# `link-not-embedding`, one line different, generates the name.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md): both
# engines were run over this corpus and diffed before any row was
# `refer(t)` does not merely TEST the target against `t`, it unifies `t`
# INTO it: referring to something as a Service makes it one, and if it
# cannot be, the conflict is an ordinary located error. Check-only
# semantics would be non-monotone -- true, then false as the target
# grows -- and the lattice guarantee is that more information never
# `flow-reaches-every-position` is the row that made the identity
# merge's apply walk substitute BEFORE its cycle guard rather than
# after: two positions of one entity hold the same object once a pass
# has merged them, so a guard that ran first left the second position
# Integrity is a UNIFICATION-time property, not a vet-time one. Within
# one evaluation the document-set is fixed, so existence IS decidable:
# a refer residuates while an entity might still be declared -- by a
# later conjunct, include or spread, as `link-forward` shows -- and the
# LAST pass is where the question is answered.
# An address is an entity name, optionally followed by a dot-separated
# path INSIDE that entity. The no-dots rule on ids makes the split
# unambiguous. Only a STRING can be one, and a malformed address is
# refused at once rather than deferred: no later pass can repair it.
# A kind or a regex conjoined with a refer is not an address, but it is
# a perfectly good constraint ON one. Those are HELD on the residual
# until the address arrives and then meet the link -- carried there
# rather than parked in a conjunct, because a conjunct rebuilt every
# pass grows a level every pass. `two-addresses-conflict` is the row
# that proves they are not simply dropped.
# The list spread applies `refer` to every element, so a dependency
# list is a list of NAMES that the engine checks. This is the shape the
# Problem section of the design could not produce: strings that check
# nothing, or references that embed everything.
# The residual renders reparseably; a RESOLVED refer is just its
# string, so the hash form sees a link as the string it is.
# --- Two refers at one position, and the shapes a template makes -----
# `refer(A) & refer(B)` is a target that must be both, in either
# written order and with either side holding the constraints. A spread
# clone carries the residual's own state -- the type to flow, the
# address it has met -- which is what makes `&: refer()` a template
# D-1: the name half is a flat identifier (no slash, no leading digit
# or hyphen); segments AFTER the first dot are keys and may lead with
# A PATH-DEPENDENT template is cloned per destination, so the residual
# it carries — the type to flow, the address it has met — has to travel
# with the clone. A constant template is SHARED, which is why only this
# Two constraints held on ONE refer, accumulated into each other rather
# than replacing: both still meet the link when the address arrives.
# THE FLOWED TYPE IS CONCRETE AT THE TARGET. A schema flowing into a
# value must not make the value a schema -- the same reasoning as a
# reference's clone clearing marks: `refer(type(t))` says the target IS
# a t, not that it is the definition of one. Without the clearing the
# target silently stopped generating. The marks are cleared on a COPY,
# `t` being shared by every position that refers to the same thing --
# and only when there are marks to clear, because cloning an unmarked
# type would move the site an error names.
# A TYPED refer IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (use-cases/BUGS.md §19). The flow
# unifies `t` into the target, and uniting a target drives the target's
# own subtree -- so a pair that links back at each other used to flow
# into each other until the depth budget ended it, reporting
# unify_cycle on a model whose meet is a fixpoint on sight
# has this shape, so typing both ends was inexpressible and use case 01
# shipped the asymmetric workaround. A flow that would re-enter an
# entity is now skipped -- the flow it is nested in is already uniting
# that entity -- and what each contributes is unchanged, as the
# differs-each-way and cycle-of-three rows show. Parity-probed.
